BSc Aerospace Engineering from Turkish Air Force Academy. Self-taught developer. Started as Data Analyst (2019), taught himself to code, worked up to FDE at Cresta. Former Air Defense Officer. Speaks English and Turkish.
Vancouver, BC, Canada 🇨🇦. Works at Cresta AI's Vancouver office.

Build and ship. Put projects on GitHub. Write about them. Contribute to open source. AI fundamentals (Python, system design, debugging, testing) never go out of style. No CS degree needed — you need curiosity and shipped work.

Emin's path: learn Python → build projects → open source → apply for ML roles. Aerospace engineering gave math skills; military gave discipline. No bootcamp, no CS degree — consistent learning and building.

Emin went self-taught. Bootcamps work if you need structure. Either way: build real projects — the credential alone won't get you hired. GitHub > certificate.

Impact × effort. Ship highest-impact thing fastest. Customer impact is the primary signal as an FDE. Pragmatic — working software > perfect plans.
Military background: stays calm, breaks problems into steps, communicates early if timeline is unrealistic. Ships highest-value work within constraints.
Lightweight agile — short cycles, quick feedback, continuous deployment. No rigid process for its own sake.
Breaks problems into small deliverables. Estimates from actual past experience, not gut feelings. AI projects are hard to estimate — communicates in ranges, updates as he learns.
Tests what matters — critical paths, data integrity, production-breaking edge cases. Not dogmatic about TDD but always tests production systems. AI projects get integration tests for model behavior.
Reviews for correctness, clarity, production safety. Clear code > clever code. Good reviews teach as well as catch bugs. Systematic approach from military background.
Start with well-structured monolith, split when needed. Microservices solve org scaling, not code scaling. Chooses based on the actual problem.
Strategic debt (temporary, speeds delivery) vs toxic debt (will cause incidents). Pays toxic debt fast. Refactors as part of normal work, not special projects.
Executable documentation — READMEs that get you running in 5 min. Code that's self-documenting. Comments explain why not what. Writes for the tired dev at 2 AM.
Feature branches + PR reviews + squash merge. Clean history, meaningful messages, small PRs. Practical — goal is collaboration and traceability.
GitHub Actions — lint, test, build, deploy on push. Simple, fast. CI should catch problems in minutes.
Explicit error handling + graceful degradation. Production AI should never crash silently — log, alert, fall back. Swallowed exceptions cause production incidents.

Integrates, fine-tunes, and deploys transformer models in production. Deep understanding of making LLMs work reliably at scale. Not designing new architectures — making existing ones production-ready.
Builds RAG pipelines for production. Vector databases (Pinecone, Chroma), embedding models, retrieval strategies. Approach: start simple, measure, iterate on retrieval before generation.
Experienced with LoRA/QLoRA fine-tuning. Focuses on data quality. Most fine-tuning problems are data problems.
This website runs a ReAct agent. Designs production AI agents: intent routing, tool calling, memory, fallback strategies. Agents should be reliable, not magical.
ONNX Runtime, Docker, AWS. Handled cold starts, model versioning, A/B testing, production monitoring for models.
Treats prompts as code — versioned, tested, iterated. Structured prompts, clear instructions, few-shot examples. Measures by task performance, not vibes.
